subject: Can I combine CL and FL methods?

messages.author: 162afa3fcd0d3916
messages.subject: Can I combine CL and FL methods?
parts:
Hello group,
I'd like to model density for my project (with several possible covariates), but also have several plausible combinations of detection sub-models.

Would it be logical (or rather, not mathematically correct) to use CL = true to narrow the top-ranked detection submodel combos, which will then be plonked into a CL = false density model ?

My thought process is: speed up the models by using CL /narrowing down possible FL models rather than testing many plausible combos. Bit of best of both worlds? OR does this mashup fall under the same rule as "don't compare AIC between CL and FL models?"

Appreciate all feedback and direction,
Thanks
Sam

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Can I combine CL and FL methods?
parts:
Hello Sam, and welcome to the group.
Maximizing the conditional likelihood produces identical estimates of detection parameters to those from maximizing the full likelihood (apart from negligible numerical effects) if the default distribution is used for n (Poisson rather than binomial). So It seems perfectly reasonable to use CL to home in on a good detection model. Of course you cannot subsequently compare CL and full models by AIC. With secr.fit(..., details = list(distribution = "binomial")) then there may be some daylight between CL and full approaches, but very little in my experience.
Murray
